text: Learn the concepts. Build the environment. Clean it up.
textPreview: Learn the concepts. Build the environment. Clean it up.

text: Welcome learners and explain that the session moves from simple cloud concepts into six guided labs. Ask for a show of hands from anyone using Azure for the first time. Generated cover artwork created for this deck. No external factual source required.
Each idea prepares you for the next practical step
textPreview: Each idea prepares you for the next practical step

text: A small Azure environment you can explain, validate, and remove safely
textPreview: A small Azure environment you can explain, validate, and remove safely

text: Use this slide as the route map. The session follows the order shown, then finishes with hands-on validation and cleanup. Ask learners which step feels least familiar.
Rent technology services when you need them
textPreview: Rent technology services when you need them

text: Microsoft secures the cloud. You secure what you put in it.
textPreview: Microsoft secures the cloud. You secure what you put in it.

text: Define cloud computing before using service names. Explain CapEx as buying equipment and OpEx as paying for ongoing use. Clarify that the customer still owns responsibilities such as identity, data, and configuration.
The service model changes how much you manage
textPreview: The service model changes how much you manage

text: Use a housing analogy if helpful. IaaS resembles renting an empty apartment, PaaS resembles a serviced apartment, and SaaS resembles a hotel room. Avoid stretching the analogy. Ask which model gives the customer the most operating system responsibility.
Access and policy flow down through four levels
textPreview: Access and policy flow down through four levels

text: Think of folders for governance, not physical boxes
textPreview: Think of folders for governance, not physical boxes

text: Explain each level in plain language. Policies and role assignments at a higher scope can affect lower scopes. A resource group does not force all resources into one physical server or one region. Source: Microsoft Learn, Azure Resource Manager overview.

Introduce the exact lab Resource Group name. Explain that deletion removes every contained resource. Pause on the word lifecycle. Ask what could go wrong if an unrelated production resource were placed in a temporary lab Resource Group.
Choose the simplest service that fits the workload
textPreview: Choose the simplest service that fits the workload

text: Keep containers and AKS conceptual. Explain that containerization alone does not require Kubernetes. For this workshop, the VM demonstrates IaaS and App Service demonstrates PaaS.

title: A virtual machine needs supporting resources

text: A virtual machine needs supporting resources
textPreview: A virtual machine needs supporting resources

text: The VM is one part of the deployed system
textPreview: The VM is one part of the deployed system

text: Lab rule: no internet-wide RDP rule
textPreview: Lab rule: no internet-wide RDP rule

text: Explain each supporting resource before opening the VM creation page. The lab does not require signing in to the VM, so learners should choose no inbound ports unless the instructor explicitly approves a restricted rule. Source: Microsoft Learn, Windows VM quickstart.
Private address space connects the workload
textPreview: Private address space connects the workload

text: /16 is a larger range. /24 is a smaller range inside it.
textPreview: /16 is a larger range. /24 is a smaller range inside it.

text: Explain VNet first, then subnet, NIC, IP addresses, and NSG. Avoid detailed subnet mathematics. The public IP does not create access by itself. The NSG must also permit traffic. Direct internet exposure increases risk.
One account can provide several storage services
textPreview: One account can provide several storage services

text: Lab choice: private Blob container with LRS
textPreview: Lab choice: private Blob container with LRS

text: LRS keeps local copies. ZRS spreads copies across zones. GRS also copies data to another region.
textPreview: LRS keeps local copies. ZRS spreads copies across zones. GRS also copies data to another region.

text: Explain Blob as object storage for files. Keep the container private. Mention that storage account names are globally unique and allow only lowercase letters and numbers. Source: Microsoft Learn, Azure Storage redundancy and Blob portal quickstart.
Authentication confirms identity. Authorization grants access.
textPreview: Authentication confirms identity. Authorization grants access.

text: Least privilege: grant only the access needed for the task
textPreview: Least privilege: grant only the access needed for the task

text: Introduce Microsoft Entra ID as the identity system. Explain Reader, Contributor, and Owner in simple terms. Students must not change RBAC in the bootcamp environment. Ask why Owner would be excessive for someone who only needs to view resources.
A managed platform for websites and APIs
textPreview: A managed platform for websites and APIs

text: Contrast IaaS and PaaS responsibilities. The Web App receives an HTTPS hostname. The App Service plan supplies compute. ZIP deployment requires index.html at the package root. Source: Microsoft Learn, Deploy files to Azure App Service.
Azure records health, performance, and changes
textPreview: Azure records health, performance, and changes

text: Find a successful resource creation event in the Resource Group Activity Log
textPreview: Find a successful resource creation event in the Resource Group Activity Log

text: Clarify that Activity Log records control-plane changes, not the content of application requests. Ask learners to name one event they expect to see after completing the labs.
Every resource has a lifecycle and a cost consequence
textPreview: Every resource has a lifecycle and a cost consequence

text: VMs and App Service plans can charge while idle. Cleanup ends the lab.
textPreview: VMs and App Service plans can charge while idle. Cleanup ends the lab.

text: Do not quote prices because they vary by region, agreement, and date. Explain that students may not have permission to create budgets. Stopping a VM is not the same as deleting its disk, public IP, or other resources.
If the VM deployment runs long, inspect the prepared VM and continue
textPreview: If the VM deployment runs long, inspect the prepared VM and continue

text: Set expectations before the labs. Keep the clock visible. Ask learners to stop and raise a hand if their subscription or region differs. Use the prepared VM if deployment remains incomplete after the planned checkpoint.
All lab resources live inside one Resource Group
textPreview: All lab resources live inside one Resource Group

text: Walk through the topology from left to right. Ask learners to point to the resources that belong to networking, storage, and web hosting. Reinforce that one cleanup action targets the complete Resource Group.
Read the first specific error before changing settings
textPreview: Read the first specific error before changing settings

textPreview: No anonymous Blob or open RDP

text: Ask the instructor before changing scope, role, region, or security rules.
textPreview: Ask the instructor before changing scope, role, region, or security rules.

text: Model calm troubleshooting. Check subscription, exact resource, and deployment details. Do not make unnecessary RBAC changes. Do not weaken network or storage security to make an error disappear.
Delete the exact Resource Group and verify the result
textPreview: Delete the exact Resource Group and verify the result

text: Deleting a Resource Group permanently deletes every resource inside it
textPreview: Deleting a Resource Group permanently deletes every resource inside it

text: Read the warning aloud. Learners must inspect the Resource Group before deletion and stop if anything looks unfamiliar. The final CLI result should be false. Source: Microsoft Learn, Delete Azure Resource Groups.
